newsitem.title: JAPAN: Canadian PM says has support for Zaire food drop.
newsitem.headline: Canadian PM says has support for Zaire food drop.

text.p: A senior Canadian official in Zaire has secured an agreement with local forces to air-drop food for thousands of Rwandan refugees and Zaireans fleeing fighting in the east of the country, Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien said on Friday.
He told a news conference that the leader of the intervention force proposed by Canada, Lieutenant-General Maurice Baril, had secured agreement with Tutsi forces in east Zaire.
"Lieutenant-General Baril...is in east Zaire and he has managed to negotiate with the belligerents on that side," said Chretien, who arrived in Japan on Tuesday for a five-day official visit.

"General Baril met with the commander of the force in that area, had some discussion with the combatants there and they have agreed to collaborate to make sure that there is no problem, " Chretien said.
On Thursday, the Zairean government categorically rejected the Canadian air-drop proposition.
"The Zairean government is categorically opposed to the Canadian proposition to drop foodstuffs for refugees and displaced Zaireans," Information Minister Boguo Makeli said in Kinshasa.
Boguo said Zaire was worried about the safety of such air drops and the fact that they would be staged from neighbouring countries it accuses of aggression.
Chretien acknowledged that care had to be taken to ensure the food drops did not cause new problems.
"Of course it has to be done with some care. Otherwise, it could lead to people using the food as a tool in the fight," he said.

Aid agencies estimated that there were 1.2 million refugees in eastern Zaire before the mass return in mid-November, prompted by fighting in the area between the rebels, Zairean troops and Rwandan Hutu extremists in the refugee camps.
